title: Entomophthorales Culturing to Sequencing v1
author: Alex Lando
materials: Our lab follows the Lovett lab CTAB protocol along with NEB Monarch HMW gDNA Extraction Kit.

steps.title: Sterilize biological safety cabinet
steps.instruction: Turn on the BSC blower, UV‑sterilize for 30 minutes, turn off UV, then wipe interior with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Collect and document cadavers
steps.instruction: Bring insect cadavers from field collection into the BSC, record metadata, and photograph each cadaver with a dissecting scope.

steps.title: Examine cadaver for fungal structures
steps.instruction: Microscopically search the cadaver and document presence of rhizoids, conidiophores, and resting spores.

steps.title: Remove cadaver from substrate
steps.instruction: Remove the mycosed cadaver from its substrate (leaf, bark, rock, etc.); if complete removal is impossible, remove as much surrounding substrate as possible.

steps.title: Place cadaver in sterile dish
steps.instruction: Position the cadaver in the centre of a sterile empty petri dish.

steps.title: Add filter‑paper ring
steps.instruction: Place a sterile ring of filter paper around the edge of the dish, ensuring it does not touch the cadaver.

steps.title: Moisten filter paper
steps.instruction: Using a 1000 µL pipette tip, add water to the filter paper until it is coated but not pooling; avoid any water contacting the cadaver.

steps.title: Seal and incubate plate
steps.instruction: Parafilm the plate carefully without jostling it and incubate for approximately 24 hours.

steps.title: Monitor for spore discharge
steps.instruction: Observe the dish until spores are shot out from the cadaver and become visible on the lid of the petri dish.

steps.title: Cut media square for spore transfer
steps.instruction: In the BSC, cut a small square out of a SDAYEYM plate with a sterile scalpel.

steps.title: Rub spores onto media square
steps.instruction: Quickly rub the media square against the lid area where spores are present, keeping the plates open as briefly as possible.

steps.title: Sandwich media onto original plate
steps.instruction: Place the media square back onto the original plate in a new area, sandwiching the spore‑bearing side between the cut piece and the plate media.

steps.title: Incubate for fungal growth
steps.instruction: Incubate the assembled plates; visible growth should appear between 48 and 96 hours.

steps.title: Perform monthly subcultures
steps.instruction: Continue transferring cultures as needed to maintain them, approximately on a monthly schedule.

steps.title: Record sample in ARSEF
steps.instruction: Transfer one clean, untouched plate to a new container and input the sample and all metadata into the ARSEF database.

steps.title: Prepare solid culture for liquid transfer
steps.instruction: When substantial growth covers the surface of the solid media, move the culture to liquid media while keeping the original solid plate and a backup.

steps.title: Prepare flasks with media
steps.instruction: Prepare two 150 mL flasks; add 25 mL Grace’s insect media and 1 mL liquid fetal bovine serum (FBS) to each.

steps.title: Harvest fungal tissue from plate
steps.instruction: Cut a square from the solid culture plate and scrape/peel the fungal material (taking minimal SDAYEYM media if necessary).

steps.title: Inoculate liquid flasks
steps.instruction: Cut the harvested fungal piece into 3‑4 smaller fragments and deposit each fragment into the two flasks using a sterile tool (repeat for the second flask).

steps.title: Shake liquid cultures
steps.instruction: Place both flasks on a shaker at room temperature for approximately 1 week.

steps.title: Harvest and centrifuge culture
steps.instruction: When significant hyphal growth is visible, remove flasks from the shaker, pour both 25 mL cultures into a single 50 mL Falcon tube, and centrifuge at 4000 g for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Remove supernatant and aliquot pellet
steps.instruction: After pelleting, pour off the Grace’s media supernatant and transfer the pellet into 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes, filling three to four tubes about halfway.

steps.title: Freeze pellets and cover with foil
steps.instruction: Remove the tubes from liquid nitrogen, open each lid, cover the tube with foil, and poke five holes in the foil using sharp forceps.

steps.title: Lyophilize frozen pellets
steps.instruction: Place the tubes on a rack in a lyophilizer (run under the “AUTO” option per fungal protocol) for 48 hours.

steps.title: Check dryness and store
steps.instruction: After 48 hours, if the tissue is light‑colored and dry, remove from the lyophilizer and store at –80 °C until DNA extraction.

steps.title: Extract high‑molecular‑weight DNA
steps.instruction: Use the lyophilized material for a high‑molecular‑weight gDNA extraction protocol of choice; use one tube for extraction and keep a backup at –80 °C.

steps.title: Relax extracted DNA
steps.instruction: Store the extracted DNA at 4 °C overnight, then relax it once daily for three consecutive days.

steps.title: Pipette DNA slowly
steps.instruction: Pipette the DNA up and down VERY SLOWLY using a wide‑bore 1000 µL tip.

steps.title: Incubate DNA at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the DNA solution at 37 °C for 1 hour.

steps.title: Repeat relaxation cycle
steps.instruction: Return the tube to 4 °C until the next day, then repeat the slow pipetting and 37 °C incubation steps; continue this cycle for a total of three days.

steps.title: Quantify DNA with Qubit
steps.instruction: After three days, run a Broad Range Qubit assay using 2 µL of sample taken from the top, middle, and bottom of the Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Prepare DNA for sequencing
steps.instruction: Calculate the required DNA amount per sequencing‑facility guidelines and transfer that volume into a screw‑cap sequencing tube.

steps.title: Seal tubes for transport
steps.instruction: Double‑seal the tubes in a Ziploc bag placed inside an empty pipette tip box.

steps.title: Pack with cooling material
steps.instruction: Add an ice pack and scrap paper to the bag to prevent jostling and keep the sample cool during transit.

steps.title: Label and ship samples
steps.instruction: Print a shipping label, cover the box with clear packing tape, and deliver the package to FedEx.

steps.title: Handle contamination events
steps.instruction: If contamination appears, excise a small clean section of culture and place it side‑down onto a PDA plate.

steps.title: Rescue culture via PDA
steps.instruction: Allow Entomophthorales to shoot spores on the PDA plate within a few days, then repeat steps 10‑13 using the PDA plate lid before transferring back onto SDAYEYM media.

steps.title: Freeze DNA tubes instantly
steps.instruction: Drop the Eppendorf tubes into liquid nitrogen to freeze instantly, preserving gDNA quality.

steps.title: Test DNA relaxation
steps.instruction: Run the DNA relaxation test as described in the machine manual (use the “AUTO” option) to confirm even relaxation throughout the tube.
